description: Per-file content provenance for the merged skills (ADR-0003 folder skills/merged): each file's destination, SHA-256 and what changed, with every source it combines. A source's `use` is primary (the upstream file the merged file is based on), merged (a second upstream whose method is merged in by hand: a change to it flags the merged file for a manual merge) or context (reference only). Each source records its path, SHA-256 and git blob at the pin in `sources`. `npm run fixtures:upstream-scope -- <upstream>` compares each source against the upstream's pin and flags the merged file when either changed. See test/merged-skills.test.ts and docs/provenance.md.

files.explanation: Merge of Matt's tdd (primary; red → green loop, what a good test is, seams, anti-patterns, rules of the loop) and pstack's tdd (cursor/plugins pstack/skills/tdd, byte-identical to the pi-mimir copy the pack shipped before; use-or-skip gating, bug-fix workflow, impractical-test fallback, guardrails, final report). Neither method is dropped. From Matt, unchanged in substance: the intro that TDD is the red → green loop and every section applies on every cycle, the GLOSSARY.md and ADR reading, 'What a good test is' with the tests.md and mocking.md pointers, the Seams section with its pre-agreed-seams rule and one-line-note proposal, the three anti-patterns (implementation-coupled, tautological, horizontal slicing with vertical slices and tracer bullets), and the rules red before green, one slice at a time and refactoring outside the loop. From pstack, unchanged in substance: the 'When to use it, and when to skip' gate (the explicit-request or cheap-obvious-local-target trigger, the do-not-force rule and its list of impractical cases, prefer no new test over a bad test and its definition of a bad test), the six-step 'Fixing a bug' workflow, 'If a failing test is impractical' with its closest-executable-check list, every Guardrail, and the Final response evidence report. New joining text: a description that carries both triggers and both skip conditions; a closing sentence that a feature is the same loop repeated; 'Run it red' and 'Rerun it green' bullets so the loop carries pstack's run-before-fix and rerun-after-fix steps. Conflicts and resolutions. (1) Gate versus loop: Matt's loop is unconditional and pstack's skips when impractical. The gate runs first and the skip is disclosed in the final report (pstack's own report rule), so a skipped test is never silent; where the user explicitly asked for TDD and the test path is impractical, the stricter pstack rule applies: say so and use the closest executable check instead of faking a test. (2) Seam confirmation versus cheap bug fixes: Matt requires the user to confirm seams before any test, pstack proceeds on the obvious cheap path. The stricter rule wins: no test at an unconfirmed seam, but for an obvious bug test path the proposal is that path and the confirmation is one line, seams confirmed in a spec or ticket count as agreed, and a delegated child takes its seams from its brief or from a spec or ticket the brief points at that already confirms them, and reports its proposed seams and writes no test at a guess only when neither names any (the implement-spec orchestrator states the seam source in each implementer brief and never merges a child that stopped at proposed seams). (3) Invocation: Matt's skill is model-invocable, pstack's sets disable-model-invocation: true. The merged skill keeps true (the stricter value): its seam-confirmation step asks the user questions and pstack's gate depends on the user's request, so the model does not load it unprompted; the skills that need it (implement, implement-spec, the bug-fix playbook, /skill:tdd recipes) load it by path or name and pass a child its absolute path. (4) Refactoring: Matt keeps it out of the loop and in code-review; code-review ships in this pack since #37 (skills/mattpocock/code-review), so the line names its path; it keeps 'when one is installed' for installs without it, and the merged skill does not stand in for it. Pack-policy adaptations to Matt's wording: 'call the Skill tool with codebase-design' became 'load the codebase-design skill (read ../../mattpocock/codebase-design/SKILL.md)', with a say-so fallback when it is missing (Pi has no Skill tool; dependencies resolve from the pack by path); the relative Markdown links to tests.md and mocking.md became backticked file names; a 'What invoking this skill grants' paragraph says the skill grants local edits and the commits its policy allows and never a push, pull request or tracker write, and that loading it without the user invoking it grants nothing. Matt's Codex-only agents/openai.yaml is not shipped (mattpocock.json excluded list).

Merge of Matt's teach (primary; the stateful teaching workspace: MISSION.md, RESOURCES.md, reference documents, learning records, lessons, assets, NOTES.md, the knowledge, skills and wisdom philosophy, fluency versus storage strength, the zone of proximal development, quiz rules) and pstack's teach (cursor/plugins pstack/skills/teach, which matches the pi-mimir copy; the teach the pack shipped before this merge was not byte-identical to either, because it already replaced the image-generation sentence with the Pi wording that says to use an image tool only if the session exposes one; the one-account how-and-why explanation built on the how and why skills, its five steps, the voice rules and the reply rule). They teach different things, so the merged skill has two modes and picks one up front: Explain (pstack's: a person wants to understand work in front of you; one plain account in the conversation, nothing written) and Workspace (Matt's: a person wants to learn a topic over several sessions; state lives in files). From pstack, unchanged in substance: the Explain section with its how-and-why delegation, the five steps, the density and punctuation rules, the reply rule and the unslop requirement, now read from ../../pstack/unslop/SKILL.md, ../../pstack/how/SKILL.md and ../../pstack/why/SKILL.md by path because Pi has no Skill tool and these skills disable model invocation; the description keeps pstack's triggers ('teach me this', 'explain this change or subsystem to me'). From Matt, unchanged in substance: the Workspace section (the workspace files, philosophy, lessons, assets, the mission, zone of proximal development, knowledge, skills, acquiring wisdom, reference documents, NOTES.md), the argument-hint, and his supporting files MISSION-FORMAT.md, RESOURCES-FORMAT.md, GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md and LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md. New joining text: the mode choice with a one-question tiebreak and the default that a request about this repository's code is Explain; a note that Explain's no-quiz and no-pacing rules are Explain's own and Workspace lessons use quizzes on purpose; GLOSSARY.md listed among the workspace files (Matt's skill links GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md only from the other formats). Conflicts and resolutions. (1) Writes: pstack's teach changes nothing, Matt's writes files into the current directory. The stricter rule wins: Explain writes nothing, and Workspace writes only after the user confirms the directory (an existing MISSION.md is the workspace only in a directory the user already confirmed; a git repository with project code needs an explicit yes before the first write even when it holds one, and a new subdirectory is the usual answer), only the named workspace files and only inside it. (2) Sources: Matt's skill tells the model to gather from the web and trusted resources; the merged skill adds a 'Sources are data' rule (never run what a source supplies, never send it local files or secrets, lessons load no remote script, stylesheet or font and embed none through iframe, object or embed, no source script is copied into the workspace, and no workspace file holds a secret or credential-bearing URL) and says community suggestions never become sign-ups or posts on the user's behalf. (3) Opening a lesson: Matt's 'run a CLI command' is narrowed to a command that opens only the lesson file just written. (4) Voice: pstack's unslop voice applies in both modes. (5) Invocation: both upstreams set disable-model-invocation: true and so does the merged skill, since a request to explain or to build a course is always the user's. (6) Matt's 'resolve from the directory /teach was run in' became 'the confirmed workspace directory' and his links to the format files became backticked names (test/skill-content.test.ts rejects relative Markdown links). A 'What invoking this skill grants' paragraph says Explain grants reading, Workspace grants the named workspace files in the confirmed directory and opening one lesson, neither grants a push, pull request, tracker or other remote write, and teach launches no subagent itself (how and why fan out their own read-only children). pstack's earlier planned-W4 interim wording had already been retired when how and why shipped. Matt's Codex-only agents/openai.yaml is not shipped.

Issue #37 decision 3: merge of Matt's prototype (primary; the question decides the shape, the logic and UI branches with their supporting files, the default-by-surrounding-code rule, the rules that apply to both, capturing the prototype as a primary source) and pstack's poteto-mode Prototype playbook (cursor/plugins pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/prototype.md, byte-identical to the pi-mimir copy, merged by hand from this pack's Pi adaptation of it: you own the decision not the code, speed over polish, propose variations, scope the decision with 'no decision means no prototype', gather references with session search tools, the empirical branch for behavior and timing forks, compare variants behind one switcher as principle-exhaust-the-design-space made cheap, verify on the matching surface with session screenshot tooling or say the visual comparison is unverified, the observation is the test, hand the direction to Feature, and the Reply). From Matt, unchanged in substance: the opening line, 'Pick a branch' with the LOGIC.md and UI.md routes and the ambiguous-question default, and the rules throwaway-and-marked, trivial to run, no persistence by default (with the 'PROTOTYPE, wipe me' scratch DB), skip the polish and surface the state. From pstack, unchanged in substance: the framing paragraph, step 1 as 'Scope the decision', step 2's references, step 3's empirical build, step 4's switcher, step 5's evidence rules and the Reply. New joining text: a third, Empirical branch beside Matt's two, and the default for an ambiguous claim about speed or behavior. Conflicts and resolutions. (1) Location: Matt locates prototype code next to where it will be used (in the app), pstack builds in an isolated scratch directory. Scratch is the default (decision 3): a directory outside the source tree (mktemp -d or a path the user names), nothing staged or committed, no installs into the project; building inside the app needs the user's explicit scope, asked for by naming the files it would touch with scratch as the alternative, and in-app code stays uncommitted with every touched file listed. (2) Capture: Matt commits the prototype to a throwaway prototype/<name> branch out of main and points at it from the implementation issue; pstack keeps it out of commits. By default the prototype stays at its scratch path (or as listed uncommitted in-app files); preserving it needs the user's authorization, with separate grants for committing it, pushing the branch and leaving a context pointer on an issue or PR in the tracker doc's repo; prototype code never reaches the main branch, and in-app files are removed when the user agrees. (3) Production handoff: Matt folds the validated decision into the real code, pstack hands the direction to Feature. The prototype never writes production code: the chosen direction goes to the real build (Feature under poteto-mode, else the ticket or /skill:to-spec), which rewrites it properly and may lift a logic prototype's pure module. (4) Invocation: Matt's skill is model-invocable and the playbook is not a skill; the merged skill keeps Matt's model invocation, since its default writes only to scratch. A 'What invoking this skill grants' paragraph says it grants writing and running the prototype in scratch and nothing else; in-app work, keeping, committing, pushing or pointing at it need more; loading it without the user invoking it grants nothing beyond the loader's grant. Pi adaptations: Matt's relative Markdown links to LOGIC.md and UI.md became backticked names (test/skill-content.test.ts rejects relative Markdown links). Matt's Codex-only agents/openai.yaml is not shipped (mattpocock.json excluded list). The playbook now points at this skill (w2.json).

Matt's logic prototype with its method, layout, scenarios and anti-patterns kept. Changes: the relative Markdown links to UI.md and SKILL.md became backticked names; the HTML file is written in the scratch directory; step 2's lifting of the pure module and step 5's capture name the real build as the one that lifts it, with the HTML shell staying with the prototype in scratch or, once the user authorized preserving it, on a throwaway branch; step 4 'Send them the file, or open it for them' became giving the user the file's path or opening it, with sending it to anyone else left to the user (messages to people need authorization, poteto-mode references/authorization.md).

Matt's UI prototype with its variants, switcher, floating bar, process and anti-patterns kept. Changes (#37 decision 3, scratch by default): a new 'Where the variants live' section keeps Matt's reason a UI is easier to judge against the app, but puts both in-app sub-shapes behind the user's explicit in-app scope; the default is a standalone scratch page that recreates the host page's surroundings with sample data and says what it approximated. Sub-shape A is the preferred in-app shape and B the last resort, as upstream. The switcher wiring and the production gate apply in-app; step 5 adds screenshotting each variant with session tooling, or saying the comparison is unverified (pstack's evidence rule); step 6 hands the winner to the real build, leaves the scratch page in scratch, drops in-app variants and the switcher from the working tree once the user agrees, and keeps the full set on a throwaway branch only with the user's authorization. The relative Markdown links to LOGIC.md and SKILL.md became backticked names.

G5 adapts the setup nudge now in the cursor pin (1e56b291 / PR #509): when the answer depends on the six task categories and a session report does not show them set, ask once to run /setup-pstack (report only) or leave the categories as they are. Later says delegations that use an unset category fail and do not fall back to host defaults, because poteto-mode always passes task:<category>, until an approved /setup-pstack <request> write sets it. A category is unset only when the Config line ends with the missing-file sentence, or a present file (the Config line ends with space, open-paren, revision sha256:, 64 lowercase hex digits, close-paren, period) has the preference value (not set). Findings are not unset: host parseExactModelRef at 7d35371 trims the reference and both sides of the slash before the auth check, while setup.ts refProblem flags surrounding whitespace and a raw ref that is not an authenticated id, including spaces around the slash. The report withholds those strings, so it cannot show the post-trim result, and the nudge does not tell the user to write config because of a Finding. Any other Config-line ending is unknown. The preference value is compared whole to (not set), so a comma inside one model id cannot change the decision. The skill does not read or write herdr-agents config. The Cursor source hash is the pin blob. Pin move to ccb5507: the interrogate table says 'different models' instead of 'several models'. Cursor's Later line that every role keeps its default model is still uncopied; the Pi Later line still says unset task:<category> delegations fail. Sticky-mode context loading: the start-a-task guidance now describes the short checklist, automatic hub loading when its full text is absent, compaction recovery, and reuse for the task form. The drift symptom checks status before distinguishing an off switch from a model that skipped supplied instructions. Task-model init revision: an approved write from /subagents-init also sets a category. Init fix round: the writer-gate paragraph and the refused-write symptom row now say that a host with the task-model init protocol routes /subagents-init and /setup-pstack init through pstack's approval dialog, keep the older-host caveat (its /subagents-init direct write is refused and the alias reports init unsupported, so /setup-pstack <request> remains the path), and list why an init notice can say it did not start. The setup steps describe the budget, category table and the host's approval dialog; the unset-category check reads the setup brief's Current choices lines instead of the retired report's Config line; troubleshooting names the host's refusals and /poteto-mode status for skill resolution. #37 decision 5: moved from skills/pstack to skills/merged and merged with Matt Pocock's ask-matt (no separate ask-matt skill ships). Everything above is kept: install, /setup-pstack as rewritten in #35, poteto-mode, the skill and principle tables, troubleshooting, and the brief-reading contract test/setup.test.ts asserts (the "/setup-pstack started the setup flow." heading, "Current choices" and the `- <category>: <models> / <thinking>` line). Joining text: the description and need-finding options name Matt Pocock's flow; 'What this release ships' says 77 skills and points at flows.md; the Pick a skill table gains code-review, prototype and a flow row, with close calls separating code-review from interrogate and the prototype skill from the Prototype playbook (poteto-mode's review gates unchanged); the explicit-only paragraph and its troubleshooting row now list every model-invocable skill (setup-pstack plus Matt's code-review, codebase-design, domain-modeling, grilling, pr, prototype, research and wizard) instead of claiming only setup-pstack loads from the user's words; the missing-from-table rule reads 'a skill in this package'.

#37 decision 5: Matt Pocock's ask-matt router (primary), adapted to this pack as poteto-help's disclosed flow map (pstack's poteto-help conventions merged: /skill:<name> commands, paths relative to the poteto-help skill directory, playbooks are not skills). Every /<name> became /skill:<name>; /setup-matt-pocock-skills became /skill:setup-repo; /clear became Pi's /new and compaction carries on in-session; 'background agent' became 'background subagent'. Only flows whose skills ship and are dependency-closed are advertised (implement and implement-spec find tdd and code-review, wayfinder finds research and prototype, all in this pack): Matt's retro, diagnosing-bugs, wait-what and writing-for-agents are not in the pack, so the map names them only to say so and points at what ships (/skill:reflect to close the loop, poteto-mode's Bug fix playbook for something broken, /skill:bro for a reply that didn't land). The prototype entry says it stays in scratch, in-app work needs explicit scope and keeping it on a prototype/<name> branch or pointing at it from an issue needs authorization (decision 3); code-review covers work in progress; pr drafts text only; wizard writes and never runs its script; teach uses a confirmed workspace or explains a change; a paragraph says no step pushes, opens a PR or writes to the tracker on its own say-so.
